ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Plant cell suspension culture technology has already been applied in production. An interest group tried to use this technology to culture carrot cells and obtain lycopene, and designed the following experimental process and culture device (as shown in the figure). Question: Should the aeration tube in the device be placed above or below the liquid surface?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left side of the figure is the experimental process, showing carrot taproot explants forming callus through dedifferentiation, then forming suspended cells through enzyme treatment, and carrying out cell culture to obtain lycopene. The right side of the figure is the cell culture device. Inside the culture vessel there is culture medium, a stirring impeller, and dispersed cells. The device is labeled with a feed inlet, pH meter, aeration port, aeration tube, and discharge outlet. Reasoning: During plant cell suspension culture, cells are dispersed in the liquid medium, and air or oxygen needs to be introduced directly into the culture medium to meet the cells' aerobic respiration; bubbles together with stirring also help maintain cell suspension. If the aeration tube is located above the liquid surface, the gas cannot effectively enter the culture medium. Therefore, the aeration tube should extend below the liquid surface.
